Definition: The primary product-owned control that returns structured allow, deny, or application-level ask decisions for governed tool use.
Structured permission decision record carrying decisionId, sessionId, toolName, decision, reason, source, decidedAt, and optional safe metadata.
Permission mode that prefers pre-approved read tools and denies write/edit/bash/network-capable and unexpected tools.
Permission mode allowing governed writes only after write hooks pass and path/symlink policy is satisfied.
Non-interactive denial posture mode; unknown and unapproved actions deny without prompting.
Permission mode where the application mediates interactive approval and persists the decision before the SDK callback returns allow or deny.
Developer-local-only mode, never shipped as ordinary behavior, still subject to Chirality denies.
Controlling rule that any explicit deny from policy, path containment, hook, governance, SDK deny rule, or human gate makes the final decision deny.
SDK convenience auto-approval list that is not a restriction boundary and cannot bypass deny policy.
Application-level approval mediation mechanism that persists the human/UI decision before returning SDK allow or deny.
Persisted evidence record for governed tool attempts including decision source, reason, and safe SDK metadata.
Source-state warning flag on docs/PRD.md (REF-006) requiring PRD-derived details to be treated as warning-qualified evidence until reconciled.
Product-owned JSONL event surface used for persisted permission evidence when the owning writer contract is available.
CONTRACT Section 1.6 invariant establishing deny-overrides-allow hard-deny precedence.
In-process Chirality MCP tools that must pass through the same overlay permission evaluation as SDK built-ins.
